paraphrase: 'See these ten goddesses, my forms, called the Mahāvidyās: Kālī, Tārā, Ṣoḍaśī, Bhuvaneśvarī, Bhairavī, Chinnamastā, Sundarī, Bagalāmukhī, Dhūmāvatī and Mātaṅgī.' Kālī stands naked before him, dark Tārā in the sky above, Chinnamastā to the right, Bhuvaneśvarī to the left, Bagalāmukhī behind, Dhūmāvatī in the south-east, Sundarī in the south-west, Mātaṅgī in the north-west, Ṣoḍaśī in the north-east, and Satī herself as Bhairavī in his body; all the Mahāvidyās give liberation to worshippers and accomplish the magical acts they desire; this is secret and not to be revealed.
notes: This list names Sundarī and Ṣoḍaśī separately and omits Kamalā — it differs from the Muṇḍamālā list quoted in the Tantrasāra. paraphrase: Śiva, seeing Satī dark and fearsome, asks who she is; Satī: 'I am the subtle Nature, born to Dakṣa as golden-limbed to win you, the supreme Person; when you three — Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva — were born, I came to you in the form of a corpse; the other two ignored me in that deformed shape, you alone took me, so I am yours. When I hear you blamed I must abandon this body.'

paraphrase: Satī explains creation: seeing that creation would not occur, the Goddess divided the Person into jīva and the supreme; then the root Nature made herself threefold — māyā, vidyā and the supreme eternal one; deluding Mahāmāyā sets creation going, while as vidyā she told the three Persons to create, protect and dissolve; she made Brahmā the creator, Viṣṇu the protector and Śiva the destroyer; 'I, without the three guṇas, shine through the one with guṇas; I took refuge in you, Śiva, and in Brahmā and Viṣṇu by a portion'; the root Nature is subtler even than she.
